sentences.text: The holotype specimen DINO 16488 consists of a nearly complete skull, lower jaws, and the first four neck vertebrae.
Four skulls of this animal are known, two of which are very complete, all measuring approximately 50 cm in length and 25 cm in height.
This giant dinosaur measured approximately 25 meters in length, 6.5 meters in height, and weighed 25 tons.
Abydosaurus is notable for having narrow teeth, contrasting with the broader teeth of earlier brachiosaurids.
Thomas Holtz estimated the length of Abydosaurus to be 18.3 meters in 2012.
Abydosaurus is a brachiosaurid sauropod dinosaur known from fossils found in the Upper Lower Cretaceous rocks of northeastern Utah, United States.
The genus Abydosaurus was named in 2010 by Daniel Chure and colleagues.
The type species A. mcintoshi was named in honor of John S. McIntosh for his contributions to Dinosaur National Monument and sauropod research.
Abydosaurus is classified within the family Brachiosauridae.
The genus authority for Abydosaurus is Chure et al., 2010.
The parent group of the genus Abydosaurus is Brachiosauridae.
Fossils of Abydosaurus date to the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous, with an age of less than 104.46 ± 0.95 million years.
The Paleobiology Database records the time range of Abydosaurus as the Cenomanian, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
